tags.description: Hannah Newmarch Spiller was Zaccheus' grandaughter and wife of Thomas Newmarch, who is assumed to have built this house.The estate was bequeathed by Hannah's sister Martha Newmarch .
tags.name: Newmarch – Spiller house (1798)

tags.description: This house was built in 1855 by Augustus C. Carey, who sold it in 1865 to Captain John Hobbs, who recruited two companies of Ipswich men during the Civil War, one of which he led to the front.
tags.name: Captain John Hobbs house (est. 1855)

tags.description: "The sightly residence of Moritz B. Philipp crowns the rugged eminence known in Mr. Hubbard's day and from the earliest times as Rocky Hill. The earliest name associated with the Hill is that of Humphrey Griffin."
tags.name: Moritz B. Philipp and Jane Peterson estate (1885)
the Howard – Arthur Wesley Dow House (1680)
Whipple Riverview Place
tags.old_name: Essex County Receptacle for the Insane at Ipswich Work House

tags.description: Samuel Wade built this house as a cottage in 1845. In 1856 it was owned by S. F. Canney, whose lumber company burned at its first location by the County Street Bridge, and again at its Brown Square location.
tags.name: Samuel Wade – S. F. Canney house (1845)

tags.description: George Dexter was a prominent Ipswich photographer in the 19th Century through 1920. This classic Queen Anne house includes an outbuilding which was used by Dexter as a photography studio.
tags.name: George Dexter house (1893)

tags.description: The original house is believed to have been constructed between 1725 and 1740. The house was in poor condition and in 2003 was restored by Ipswich architect Matthew Cummings. It is identical in construction to the Dennis-Dodge house a few doors away.
tags.name: Abraham Knowlton house ( est. 1726)

tags.description: Historic home located in Ipswich, Ma. Estimated to be built around 1920.
tags.name: 14 Argilla Rd. (c. 1920)

tags.description: Joseph Bennett built this early Second Period house in 1725. In 1818 the house was sold to Capt. Sylvanus Caldwell, who engaged in maritime trade along the coast from Massachusetts to Maine for a half century.
tags.name: Bennet-Caldwell House (est. 1725)

tags.description: The simple exterior is enlivened by Victorian elements, including two door hoods with elaborate scroll brackets decorated with incised floral motifs and sunbursts. Thomas Brown is the first known owner of the house.
tags.name: Thomas and Elizabeth Brown house (c 1844)

tags.description: The first known owner of this house is Norman J. Bolles, president of the Ipswich Savings bank. This house is a fine example of a Queen Anne Cottage.
tags.name: Norman J. Bolles house (c 1900)

tags.description: The house at 15 County Street was built in 1788 and is Federal in style. Rev. Levi Frisbie was Rev. Lev. Frisbie, who was installed as pastor of First Church in Ipswich on Feb. 7, 1776. He remained in that post for thirty years, and this was his home.
tags.name: Rev. Levi Frisbie house (est. 1788)

tags.description: This house was built in 1843 near the EBSCO dam as Hoyt’s Veneer Mill. It was moved in 1859 to its present location where it became the Perkins & Daniels Stocking Factory. Farley & Daniels succeeded in 1884.
tags.name: Daniels Shoe Factory (est. 1843)
